title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In cote 140-3 Grothendieck studies a profinite group M, a 'Teichmüller–Galois' type group of automorphisms built on the profinite completion Gl(2,Z)^ and its generators rho, sigma, tau. It is compared with auxiliary groups M_{rho,sigma} and with their quotients Gamma_{rho,sigma} = M_{rho,sigma}/G^+_{rho,sigma}. Earlier pages give the following facts.

- (56) gives an isomorphism M ≅ M^{⇆}_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho ⊂ M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho.
- (57)–(58) are exact sequences. One of them is 1 → G^+ → M → Pi~_Q → 1, where Pi~_Q ≅ gamma_{rho,sigma}.
- (59) is the extension 1 → SZ_rho × SZ_sigma (= L_rho × L_sigma) → Gamma_{rho,sigma} → gamma_{rho,sigma} → 1. It has a 'bisection' Gamma^{⇆}_{rho,sigma} whose intersection with L_rho × L_sigma is mu_rho × 1.

This page states the consequence as formula (60) (the page number on the image reads (60), not (56)).

(i) Gamma_{rho,sigma} = Gamma^{⇆}_{rho,sigma} · SGamma_{rho,sigma}, with SGamma = SZ_rho × SZ_sigma = L_rho × L_sigma and Gamma^{⇆} ∩ SGamma = mu_rho.

(ii) Dividing by mu_rho (implicitly normal, indeed central, in Gamma) gives an honest semidirect product decomposition: Gamma_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho ≅ (L_rho/mu_rho × L_sigma) ⋊ (Gamma^{⇆}/mu_rho). The complement Gamma^{⇆}/mu_rho ≅ gamma_{rho,sigma} ≅ Pi~_Q.

In modern terms, the arithmetic quotient Pi~_Q (the analogue of the image of Gal(Qbar/Q), or of a GT-hat-like group) is realised as a complement splitting the extension of gamma by the abelian(-ish) 'cyclotomic/Z-parts' L_rho × L_sigma, once mu_rho is factored out.

Grothendieck then says what he wants to do next. He wants to describe what becomes, under M ≅ M^{⇆}_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho ⊂ M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho, of the many distinguished subgroups of M introduced earlier:
- M(0) and M[0];
- M^!_0[0] and M^!!_0[0], which equal M^{G}[0], M^{Pi}[0], M^{Pi_0}[0], i.e. M(0)·L_0^{G}, M(0)·L_0^{Pi}, M(0)·L_0^{Pi_0};
- M(1/2)_rho, M'(−rho), M'''(−rho) and N^!_rho.

To do this he must first define the analogous subgroups in general M_{rho,sigma}. He announces a return to that, which is exactly the next page: 'VI. Les groupes M_{phi,sigma} généraux : récapitulation, raffinement'.

So the page is a transitional bookkeeping lemma (a semidirect product splitting) plus a plan.
errors: The previous page wrote the bisection as gamma_{rho,sigma} ≅ Gamma^{⇆}_{rho,sigma}. That is inconsistent with the stated intersection mu_rho × 1 with L_rho × L_sigma. This page silently corrects it to gamma ≅ Gamma^{⇆}/mu_rho, which is the right statement.
Normality of mu_rho in Gamma_{rho,sigma} is used implicitly in passing to Gamma/mu_rho. It is presumably true because mu_rho is central or characteristic in L_rho, but it is not stated.

ideas.what: Splitting of the extension 1 → L_rho/mu_rho × L_sigma → Gamma_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho → gamma_{rho,sigma} → 1 by the subgroup Gamma^{⇆}/mu_rho, which is identified with the 'arithmetic' group Pi~_Q
ideas.modern_name: semidirect product decomposition / section of a group extension (Galois–Teichmüller type group as complement of a cyclotomic-type kernel)
ideas.usually_credited_to: routine group theory; the ambient GT-type setting is usually credited to Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara for GT-hat
ideas.where_published: Analogous ideas (Galois–Teichmüller tower acting via SL(2,Z)^ and its quotients) appear programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme; this precise decomposition is not, to my knowledge, in published texts

ideas.what: Program to transport the distinguished subgroups M(0), M[0], M^!_0[0], M^!!_0[0], M(1/2)_rho, N^!_rho, etc. into general groups M_{rho,sigma}
ideas.modern_name: filtration/level subgroups of a GT-like group relative to a finite quotient of Gl(2,Z)^

deep.surprise_reason: A short transitional page. It records an elementary semidirect product consequence of the preceding exact sequences, correcting a small slip from the previous page, and announces the general treatment of M_{rho,sigma} carried out on the next page. Nothing new beyond the internal bookkeeping of an unpublished theory.
transcription_corrections: The formula label on this page reads '(60)', not '(56)'. It continues the numbering (56)–(59) from the previous page.

The intersection condition reads 'Gamma^{⇆}_{rho,sigma} ∩ SGamma_{rho,sigma} = mu_rho', and the subscript under SGamma is 'SZ_rho × SZ_sigma = L_rho × L_sigma'. The underbrace under Gamma^{⇆}/mu_rho reads 'gamma_{rho,sigma} ≅ Pi~_Q'.
Line 2 likely reads 'groupes remarquables' (or similar) rather than 'groupes accouplés'. The first line probably reads 'Pour dire ce que deviennent les nombreux groupes remarquables'.

The list reads M(0), M[0], M^!_0[0], M^!!_0[0], with below them '= M^{G}[0], M^{Pi}[0], M^{Pi_0}[0]' and '= M(0).L_0^{G}, M(0).L_0^{Pi}, M(0).L_0^{Pi_0}'. The middle tag is Pi, not Pi_0, and a crossed-out item precedes the last one.
In the line 'M(1/2)_rho, M'(-rho), M'''(-rho), N^!_rho de M par' there is an inserted 'Z''_sigma !' below, which is a marginal insertion of unclear role.
'les homomorphismes' could be 'l'isomorphisme'. The target is written M_{rho,sigma}, probably meant as M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho as on the previous page.
'groupes analogues' is likely correct ('il faudrait d'abord introduire les groupes analogues dans les M_{rho,sigma} généraux').
